title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
reason: Simplify over-abstract prose, remove unsafe open-flame staging, and retain accurate, useful castle vocabulary in a supervised family visit.

pages.1: Dad showed Aiden and Betty a picture of a castle. "We can visit it on Saturday," he said. Betty found a book to take with them.
pages.2: On Saturday, Mum drove. Dad sat beside her. Aiden and Betty wore their seat belts in the back. Soon, the castle appeared on the hill.
pages.3: They crossed a wooden bridge over the moat. Aiden heard each step tap on the old boards. Betty checked the picture map.
pages.4: The great hall was tall, cool, and quiet. Some floor stones were smooth from many years of footsteps. Aiden bent down to look.
pages.5: Betty held the picture map. First came the great hall. Next came the armour room. Then they would climb the tower.
pages.6: In the armour room, a guide showed them a suit of plate armour. Aiden tried on one heavy glove while the guide watched.
pages.7: Stone steps led to a dark room below the castle. Soft wall lights showed the way. Betty studied a picture board while Dad stayed close.
pages.8: The tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They walked in one line. From the top, they could see the river, town, and fields.
pages.9: "People looked from this tower long ago," Betty said. Aiden drew the wide view in his notebook.
pages.10: On the way down, Aiden found a narrow slit in the wall. A guide explained that archers could see out while staying behind thick stone.
pages.11: In the shop, Betty chose a small castle model. Aiden chose a picture book. Dad held up a funny cup. Mum laughed.
pages.12: On the drive home, Mum asked what they liked best. Aiden chose the worn floor. Betty chose the view from the tower.
pages.13: That evening, Aiden drew four things: the bridge, the hall, the narrow slit, and the view. His page helped him remember the day.
